subsystems.name: Cultivation system
subsystems.role: grows algae in shallow, continuously mixed water under sunlight.

subsystems.name: Culture management
subsystems.role: keeps a fast-growing, contamination-resistant algal population.
parts: pH, temperature and dissolved oxygen monitoring

subsystems.name: Harvesting and dewatering
subsystems.role: concentrates a very dilute culture into a thick paste.

subsystems.name: Extraction
subsystems.role: breaks open cells and separates the oil.

subsystems.name: Conversion
subsystems.role: turns algal oil into a usable fuel.
parts: hydrotreating unit (drop-in diesel and jet fuel)

subsystems.name: Residue and co-product handling
subsystems.role: recovers value from what is left after oil removal.

buildSteps.title: Screen a strain
buildSteps.detail: Collect and test local microalgae for lipid content, growth rate and tolerance of the site's temperature swings; domesticate the best candidates through repeated outdoor culture.

buildSteps.title: Choose pond or reactor
buildSteps.detail: Open raceways are cheap per hectare but give low cell density and are easily contaminated; closed photobioreactors reach higher densities but cost far more to build and run.

buildSteps.title: Build the farm
buildSteps.detail: Level and line the pond area, install paddlewheels and baffles, lay brackish-water supply and return lines, and add CO2 sparging fed from a nearby industrial or fermentation source.

buildSteps.title: Grow the culture
buildSteps.detail: Start from a clean inoculum, dose nitrogen and phosphorus, keep the water moving and monitor for grazers and invading algae that would crash the pond.

buildSteps.title: Harvest
buildSteps.detail: Add flocculant to clump the cells, float or settle them, then centrifuge the concentrate — the step where most of the processing energy is spent, because pond cultures are well under a gram of dry matter per litre.

buildSteps.title: Extract the oil
buildSteps.detail: Disrupt the cells mechanically, then extract lipids with a recovered solvent; wet-extraction routes avoid the large drying penalty.

buildSteps.title: Convert to fuel
buildSteps.detail: Transesterify the oil into biodiesel, or hydrotreat it into a drop-in diesel or jet fraction that fits existing engines and infrastructure.

buildSteps.title: Recover co-products
buildSteps.detail: Strip protein, pigments and omega-3 oils before or alongside fuel conversion, and digest the residue to make biogas and recycle nutrients back to the ponds.

prerequisites.why: in dilute pond culture the concentration step can consume more energy than the fuel delivers.
algal growth needs carbon; siting near a cement plant, power station or fermenter is what makes dosing affordable.

prerequisites.tech: Robust high-lipid strains for outdoor ponds
prerequisites.why: lab strains rarely hold productivity when exposed to real sunlight, temperature swings and invaders.
oil hydrotreating is already used commercially for other bio-oils, so algal oil could use existing refineries.
capital and operating costs per hectare still far exceed the value of the fuel produced.

pathway.milestone: hectare-scale demonstration ponds and photobioreactors, plus research programmes such as the US Aquatic Species Program that ran from 1978 to 1996
algae grown on wastewater and flue gas, with nutrients recycled from the residue
pathway.unlocks: a revenue stream from waste treatment that offsets fuel costs.

pathway.milestone: biorefineries led by high-value products — pigments, feed protein, omega-3 — with fuel as the bulk output
pathway.unlocks: a viable business before fuel reaches cost parity.

pathway.milestone: harvesting energy cut sharply and carbon pricing applied to aviation fuel
pathway.unlocks: algal jet and diesel at meaningful volumes on non-arable land with brackish water.
